family: wyrm — Godzilla (gz2014, burning, gvk, gxk, supernova)
overallRead: The row reads correctly as ONE escalating animal — every form is unmistakably the hunched plated wyrm, never confused with the flyers/hydra rows, and the palette/glow tells (charcoal+blue, orange lava, charcoal+blue+broken, pink self-lit, violet) all land the color-ID. The family's failure is NOT color — it is that the SILHOUETTE LADDER is nearly flat. At iso the five outlines are near-clones: bulk runs 1.05/1.05/1.0/0.98/1.08 (a ~5% spread no one can see at 40px) and the dorsal-ridge heights collapse into one blunt-to-medium band, with two outright INVERSIONS that actively mis-ID forms. (1) The lean ladder is backwards: gvk (effective torso ~0.93) is drawn NARROWER than gxk (~0.98), so the 'leanest agile' tier looks chunkier than the 'lean warrior' before it — the one place a real proportion change exists, it points the wrong way. (2) The endpoint doesn't tower: supernova's ridge (heightMul 1.18) is actually SHORTER on-frame than gxk's (1.2) and its bulk (1.08) barely clears gz2014 (1.05), so the 'walking supernova' reads as a slightly-spikier purple gxk instead of the biggest/tallest mass. The whole fix is a coordinated re-rank of two shape axes — torsoWidth (to make the lean ladder monotonic gz2014 wide → gvk 0.93 → gxk 0.90) and plateHeightMul/bulk (to make supernova clearly out-tower and out-mass everything). All edits are wyrm-local config.js shape{} keys plus one opt-gated draw addition (burning lead-plate); the shared helpers already honor every knob (torsoWidth via drawTorso ctx.scale, heightMul via drawPlates), so cross-family regression risk is near-zero. Bounds verified: supernova at bulk 1.13 / heightMul 1.38 puts the tallest apex at canvas-Y 6.2px — clears the 168px top with margin, no plate-count reduction needed.

forms.currentRead: The bluntest, heaviest charcoal wyrm with the shortest stubby ridge and wide legs — correctly the baseline 'reference bulk'. Reads clearly as GareGoji 2014: matte grey rock, no self-glow, short jagged fins. Its only weakness is that 'heaviest of the five' does not actually read because the bulk ladder around it is flat — but as the wide anchor it is on-spec.

topChanges.change: Leave gz2014 as the WIDE anchor of the lean ladder — do NOT add torsoWidth here. The fix for 'heaviest doesn't read' lives entirely on the leaner tiers narrowing below it (gvk 0.93 → gxk 0.90). Optionally bump bulk 1.05→1.08 ONLY if, after gxk/gvk narrow, gz2014 still doesn't read as widest; treat as a follow-up, not a first move.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Once gvk/gxk narrow, gz2014 becomes the visibly widest outline, restoring the 'heaviest bear-bulk' must-have without touching this form. The optional 1.08 only widens the gap to the warrior tiers if needed.
topChanges.regressionRisk: Very low. A bulk bump scales BH and therefore BW/legs/ridge together — verify the gz2014 plate apex (currently canvas-Y 33.5) stays well clear of the top (it does at 1.08). No effect on other forms (per-form key).

topChanges.change: Do NOT add a per-form headScaleMul. The critique's smaller-head idea is real spec but sub-threshold at 40px and would need a new fg.headScale plumb through drawHead — skip it; the existing BH*0.02 head-lowering translate already implies scale.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Avoids a shared-helper change for a delta invisible at iso.

forms.currentRead: Strong color-ID: charred near-black body with glowing orange lava fissures across chest/belly/thigh, incandescent gradient plate faces, full orange self-illum rim — unmistakably Burning Godzilla via surface. But its SILHOUETTE is a near pixel-clone of gz2014: same bulk 1.05, and with NO plateHeightMul it defaults to 1.0, so the ridge is only marginally taller than gz2014's 0.85 and has no lead-plate breaking the skyline. Disambiguation rides 100% on palette, not the spec's intended shape escalation.

topChanges.change: Add plateHeightMul:1.10 and raise plateJag 0.55→0.62 to burning's shape{}. Taller + sharper than gz2014's 0.85/0.35 so the ridge is a visible notch above baseline, re-sharpened toward 1954 jaggedness.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Burning's ridge becomes a legible escalation over gz2014 instead of an identical blunt row — the orange palette stops being the only separator. Verified apex at canvas-Y 28.2px (safe).
topChanges.regressionRisk: Low. heightMul/jag are read only by drawPlates for this form; no sibling touched. Slightly taller plates stay well inside canvas.

topChanges.change: Add ONE deterministic lead-plate spike: in drawPlates, after computing `size` (archetypes.js:268), insert `if (opts.leadPlate != null && i === Math.round(N*opts.leadPlate)) size *= 1.35;` and wire opts.leadPlate from buildWyrm's plateOpts (archetypes.js:388-391) reading shape.leadPlate; set shape.leadPlate:0.5 ONLY on burning.
topChanges.expectedEffect: One tall hot plate breaks the skyline, delivering the spec's 'one taller hot lead-plate' silhouette tell. Opt-gated so the other four forms' plate rows stay byte-identical.
topChanges.regressionRisk: Low but this is the only SHARED-HELPER edit for the family — guarded by `opts.leadPlate != null` so it's a no-op for every form that doesn't set the key. Confirm the spiked plate (×1.35 on a 1.10 base) still clears the top: at mid-row indices it does.

forms.currentRead: The one tier with a genuine encoded proportion change: torsoWidth 0.93 narrows the body, 2 broken/chipped plates give battle-scar asymmetry, 11 sharper plates, blue keylines, no body glow — reads clearly as the lean GvK warrior. The problem is purely RELATIVE: gvk only looks 'leaner' if its neighbors are wider, and gxk currently is NOT (gxk is drawn wider), so gvk's lean read is broken from the gxk side.

topChanges.change: No change to gvk's torsoWidth (0.93 is correct and load-bearing). The inversion is fixed entirely on gxk's side by adding torsoWidth:0.90 there. Keep gvk as the middle rung of the lean ladder.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Once gxk narrows to 0.90, the ladder reads monotonic: gz2014 wide → gvk 0.93 → gxk 0.90. gvk's 'leaner warrior' silhouette finally reads because the tier after it is leaner still.
topChanges.regressionRisk: None — no edit to this form for the width axis.

topChanges.change: Add plateHeightMul:1.12 and raise plateJag 0.6→0.68 to gvk's shape{} so its razor ridge stays clearly taller/sharper than gz2014 and keeps the ridge-height ladder coherent (gz2014 0.85 → burning 1.10 → gvk 1.12 → gxk 1.2 → supernova 1.38).
topChanges.expectedEffect: Prevents gvk's ridge regressing BELOW burning's raised 1.10 and sharpens the razor-maple-leaf base so 'tall sharp slim fins' reads vs gz2014's blunt stubs. Apex verified at canvas-Y 32.1px (safe).
topChanges.regressionRisk: Low. Per-form keys; drawPlates-only. Note gvk's on-frame apex stays slightly shorter than burning's because gvk's bulk is 1.0 vs burning 1.05 — acceptable, since gvk's identity tells are the torso-narrowing + broken plates, not raw ridge height.

forms.currentRead: Color and ridge density land the ID — full pink self-illum rim, 13 tall sharp plates (heightMul 1.2), pink keylines, no fissures: clearly the Evolved pink form by palette. But the BODY MASS is wrong: bulk 0.98 with NO torsoWidth makes it WIDER than gvk's effective 0.93, so the 'leanest agile form' reads as normal-or-chunky-bulk that just glows pink. Its signature 'sleekest before the nova' silhouette is absent — hence generic 'glowing pink monster' rather than specifically the lean Evolved Godzilla.

topChanges.change: Add torsoWidth:0.90 to gxk's shape{} (narrower than gvk's 0.93) and drop bulk 0.98→0.95. drawTorso already honors torsoWidth via ctx.scale (archetypes.js:199), so this is a pure config change.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Fixes the single worst silhouette inversion in the family: restores gz2014(wide) → gvk(0.93) → gxk(0.90) so gxk is visibly the leanest. Separates gxk from gvk on BUILD as well as color, killing the 'just gvk but pink' read.
topChanges.regressionRisk: Low. torsoWidth scales only the torso path horizontally; legs/head/tail unaffected. Pairs cleanly with the pink rim. Confirm the narrowed torso still tucks under the (unchanged) leg roots — at 0.90 it does.

topChanges.change: Hold gxk's plateHeightMul at 1.2 / plates 13 — do NOT raise it. It is spec-correct as 'tallest of the PRACTICAL forms'. The gxk↔supernova ridge gap is opened by raising SUPERNOVA, not by touching gxk.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Keeps gxk the spikiest practical tier while letting supernova's 1.38 clearly out-tower it (gxk apex canvas-Y 30.7 vs supernova ~6.2).

forms.currentRead: Violet body, white-violet fissures, violet self-illum rim, 16 plates — the color/crack palette IDs it as the violet endpoint and distinguishes it from pink gxk and orange burning. But its DEFINING silhouette delta is missing: the overgrown crystal spine isn't there (heightMul 1.18 is actually SHORTER on-frame than gxk's 1.2) and the bulk (1.08) barely clears gz2014 (1.05). So it reads as a slightly-spikier purple gxk, not as the biggest/tallest 'walking supernova' that dominates the frame. This is the single biggest silhouette gap in the family.

topChanges.change: Raise plateHeightMul 1.18→1.38 — the overgrown crystal spine is supernova's identity. Bounds verified: at bulk 1.13 the tallest apex lands at canvas-Y 6.2px, inside the 168px top with margin, so NO plate-count reduction is needed (count 16 is the identity).
topChanges.expectedEffect: The ridge finally towers — supernova apex ~6.2px vs gxk 30.7px opens a clear ~24px height gap, delivering the 'crystal spine pushing to the top of the frame' that separates it from gxk on silhouette.
topChanges.regressionRisk: Low but bounds-sensitive: this is the only edit that approaches the canvas top. Verified safe at 1.38×bulk1.13 (6.2px). If bulk is later pushed past 1.13, re-check; cap heightMul rather than dropping plates.

topChanges.change: Raise bulk 1.08→1.13 so supernova is unmistakably the biggest mass of the ladder. BW=BH*0.5 scales with bulk, widening AND heightening the whole figure.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Gives the 'biggest/bulkiest endpoint' read (vs gz2014 1.05 / gxk 0.95-after-fix). Combined with the 1.38 ridge, the outline becomes the towering nova mass instead of a recolored gxk.
topChanges.regressionRisk: Low. Bulk scales everything proportionally; the legMul/armMul/tail stay relative. Coordinate with the heightMul raise for the shared apex bounds-check (done: 6.2px at the combined 1.13/1.38). Back off to 1.11 only if a later change pushes the apex under 2px.

topChanges.change: Decline the tail-thickness knob. The critique's tailThick idea needs new params threaded into drawTailScaled for a polish-level delta; the bulk+ridge raises carry the mass read on their own.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Avoids a shared-helper edit for a sub-threshold gain; bulk 1.13 already thickens the whole silhouette including the tail root.

sharedHelperChanges.change: Add ONE opt-gated lead-plate spike for burning: after `var size = arc * heightMul * jH;` (line 268), insert `if (opts.leadPlate != null && i === Math.round(N*opts.leadPlate)) size *= 1.35;`. Plumb it by adding `leadPlate: (s.leadPlate != null ? s.leadPlate : null)` to the plateOpts object in buildWyrm (archetypes.js:388-391).
sharedHelperChanges.rationale: Delivers burning's 'one taller hot lead-plate breaks the skyline' silhouette tell, which no current knob provides. Keeping it in the shared helper (rather than a burning-only branch) matches the existing data-driven pattern.
sharedHelperChanges.regressionRisk: Low — fully guarded by `opts.leadPlate != null`, so it is a literal no-op for gz2014/gvk/gxk/supernova (none set shape.leadPlate); their plate rows stay byte-identical. The ×1.35 spike on burning's 1.10 base stays within canvas at the chosen index (leadPlate 0.5 → mid-row, apex well clear of top). This is the ONLY shared-helper edit required; all other fixes are config.js shape{} keys that existing helpers already honor (torsoWidth via drawTorso ctx.scale line 199, plateHeightMul/jag/broken via drawPlates).

implementationOrder: gxk: add torsoWidth:0.90 + bulk 0.98→0.95 (config.js:151) — fixes the worst inversion, makes the lean ladder monotonic gz2014>gvk>gxk; highest recognizability leverage, zero bounds risk
supernova: raise plateHeightMul 1.18→1.38 + bulk 1.08→1.13 (config.js:159) — delivers the towering crystal-spine endpoint, the family's biggest single silhouette gap; bounds pre-verified at 6.2px
burning: add plateHeightMul:1.10 + plateJag 0.55→0.62 (config.js:136) — turns the ridge escalation from color-only into shape, so burning≠gz2014 on outline
gvk: add plateHeightMul:1.12 + plateJag 0.6→0.68 (config.js:143) — keeps the ridge-height ladder monotonic and sharpens the razor base now that burning is taller

burning lead-plate: drawPlates opt-gate (archetypes.js:268) + shape.leadPlate:0.5 (config.js:136) + plateOpts plumb (archetypes.js:388) — the one shared-helper edit, adds the skyline-breaking lead plate
gz2014 (optional follow-up): bulk 1.05→1.08 (config.js:128) ONLY if, after gxk/gvk narrow, gz2014 still doesn't read as the widest mass — re-screenshot first
